research_objective: Evaluate whether SAEE can assess evidence sufficiency for defined accountability claims under controlled scenarios that more closely resemble agent tool execution, without treating the protocol as an evaluation result.

research_questions.question: How much accountability information can be supported by trace-only observations?
research_questions.planned_analysis: Measure claim-level support and unsupported-claim acceptance under the trace-only condition, stratified by claim type.

research_questions.question: How does adding structured evidence objects affect evidence adequacy evaluation?
research_questions.planned_analysis: Compare pre-registered claim and missing-evidence outcomes across trace-only, receipt, relationship, and complete-package conditions.

research_questions.question: Can SAEE identify missing evidence relationships and avoid false accountability claims?
research_questions.planned_analysis: Compare predicted missing and invalid relationships with independently annotated reference labels and report false accountability outcomes.

scenarios.unit_of_analysis: one agent task attempt paired with one accountability claim and one evidence condition

baselines.label: Observability-only approach
baselines.decision_surface: trace field presence and trace consistency

baselines.label: Receipt/log based approach
baselines.decision_surface: structured record presence and local record validity

baselines.label: SAEE evidence adequacy approach
baselines.decision_surface: claim-specific fields, evidence objects, and semantic relationships

metrics.interpretation_boundary: A lower planned value would indicate fewer false profile-support decisions in the evaluated dataset, not legal correctness or universal safety.

metrics.formula: exact_missing_set_matches / all_annotated_claim_attempts; also report set precision, recall, and F1
metrics.interpretation_boundary: Agreement is measured against protocol annotations, whose quality and ambiguity must be reported.
Coverage must be reported beside false accountability outcomes and cannot be treated as a standalone quality score.
Completeness describes recorded relationships and does not prove external authenticity, causality, or legal adequacy.

options.purpose: Controlled fault injection and known reference relationships.
Independently sourced or consenting-participant traces with documented provenance, privacy, and license review.
Realistic trace structure combined with controlled evidence omissions and relationship mutations.

limitations: No external dataset has been selected, downloaded, licensed, or evaluated.
No real agent, external tool, OpenTelemetry collector, external API, or unknown code has been run.
Baseline labels describe planned comparison logic and do not indicate completed implementations.
Metric definitions do not imply measured values or expected superiority.
The first scenario covers code-agent tool execution and may not generalize to other agent domains.
Annotation agreement targets and sample size must be confirmed through an approved pilot and preregistration.
External validation remains incomplete until independently executed and reviewed evidence exists.
